title: Token cohort tracing & span-exemplar enrichment for cost attribution
creator: Sasha Kim
description: Introduce a low-overhead, deterministic sampling strategy (token cohorts) and span-exemplar enrichment so we can attribute latency and cache impact down to token positions with bounded telemetry volume and no plaintext token leakage. The goal is accurate per-token cost signals for billing and optimizer heuristics while keeping overhead <5% CPU/ingest and respecting privacy constraints.
spec: Motivation: Full per-token tracing is prohibitively expensive at scale (ingest, storage, and runtime overhead). Existing instrumentation gives request-level and coarse emission windows. We need an approach that provides: (1) high-fidelity latency breakdowns around critical hot paths (KV cache, kernel execution, queuing), (2) signal for token-position cost curves (first tokens vs later tokens), and (3) linkage to billing events for cost modeling. Design summary: 1) Token cohorts: deterministically assign a small fraction of token emissions to cohorts based on (request_id_hash xor model_name_hash) and token_index modulo N_cohorts. Cohort sampling yields even coverage across token positions and customer surface without per-request randomization. 2) Span model: emit an "emission_window" span for contiguous emissions where each span includes attributes: token_count (int), start_token_index (int), cohort_id (string), kv_hit_count (int), kv_miss_count (int), compute_ns (int), kernel_variant (string). 3) Exemplars: sample exemplar spans for a subset of cohorts containing per-token microtimings (per token: generation_ns, kv_check_ns, kv_hit boolean, batching_wait_ns). Exemplars link to full trace via trace_id and to metrics via exemplar IDs. 4) Privacy: we NEVER emit token text or full logits. Only integer token indices, token lengths (in subtoken counts), and booleans for cache hit. 5) Overhead budget: cohort fraction defaults to 0.5% of emissions with adjustable policy: can increase to 5% in canary. 6) Backfill & migration: new schema in tracing and metrics, with adapters in ingestion pipeline to join exemplars to request-level billing events. 7) Storage: exemplars kept for 30 days; aggregated token-position histograms stored long-term for cost modeling.
tracing_format: We will extend our OTLP spans with three new semantic attributes: rwi.cohort_id, rwi.start_token_index, rwi.token_window_size. Exemplars will be represented as OTLP/span events with name 'token_exemplar' and attributes token_pos (string list encoded as comma-separated ints), timing_ns (comma-separated ints) and kv_mask (bitmask hex string). Each exemplar contains a stable exemplar_id which is added to Prometheus histogram exemplars for aggregation linking.
metrics: rwi.token_position_latency_seconds: Prometheus histogram (buckets tuned for 0-200ms) with exemplar linking to trace IDs
rwi.token_window_compute_ns: summary for per-window compute time
log_pipeline: Flow: runtime -> trace-agent -> kafka-topic 'rwi-traces' -> enrichment service -> bigquery/long-term and prometheus-exemplar forwarder. Enrichment service joins trace exemplars with request metadata (customer_id, model_variant, route) using request_id. We will add a privacy filter that strips any string attributes beyond allowed set. For cost-sensitive customers we tag traces with 'billing_scope' for downstream join in billing pipelines.
dashboards: Grafana: 'Token Position Cost Curve' panel - aggregated median/p95 latency by token index (0..128) + rolling cohort coverage
Grafana: 'KV Impact Heatmap' - per-model, per-token-index delta between kv_hit and kv_miss latencies
Grafana: 'Cohort Sampling Health' - sampling rate, exemplar ingestion lag, failed-enrichment ratio
Grafana: 'Billing Attribution Errors' - mismatches between model-estimated token cost and logged exemplars
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated in runtime with default OFF. Stage 1: internal canary (1% traffic) for 7 days. Stage 2: increase to 5% and enable Prometheus exemplars. Stage 3: customer opt-in and 25% experiment for top 10 customers to validate cost models. Stage 4: gradual enablement for all hosted traffic when metrics show low overhead and accurate joins.
Rollback: global kill-switch for cohort sampling + immediate tombstone of exemplar forwarding.
testing_plan: Unit: deterministic cohort assignment tests, exemplar encoding/decoding
Integration: run against perf harness to measure <5% CPU/ingest overhead at 5% cohort rate
E2E: synthetic requests to verify join between exemplars and billing events (end-to-end cost attribution)
Privacy: static analysis to ensure no string token content added to spans
migration_steps: Add new tracing attributes to runtime (backwards compatible) and feature-flag behind 'token_cohort_exemplars'
Deploy enrichment service, start forwarding exemplars to a staging BigQuery dataset, run joins and reconcile with historical billing samples
Flip canary and monitor Grafana dashboards and cost ingestion lag metrics
Promote schema to production and update billing pipelines to consume aggregated token-position histograms
